summary: This work demonstrates a single-step grayscale electron-beam lithography process for fabricating airbridges of varying sizes ($0.5$–$4$ µm width, $5$–$40$ µm length) that unify all electrical interconnects in superconducting circuits, eliminating the need for separate bandage contacts to Josephson junctions. Measured relaxation times exceeding $250$ µs in transmons and quality factors around $4 	imes 10^5$ in CPW resonators show that airbridges provide high-quality contacts while substantially simplifying fabrication.
motivation: Conventional superconducting circuit fabrication uses two separate types of interconnects: airbridges for non-adjacent elements and bandages for junction contacts. Bandages introduce parasitic material interfaces, increase process complexity, and expose the Si substrate to damaging Ar$^+$ ion milling during oxide removal.
method: The authors developed a unified single-step grayscale e-beam lithography process to fabricate all airbridges simultaneously, with a reduced resist height of $1$ µm (versus $3$ µm in prior work) and modified post-exposure baking and development protocols. The resist scaffold protects the junction region from ion milling damage. Room-temperature conductance measurements verified galvanic contact; CPW resonators and transmon devices characterized the performance at millikelvin temperatures.
result: Junction-contacting airbridges ($5$ µm length, $3$ µm width) achieved $>99\%$ yield; grounding airbridges ($36$ µm length, $4$ µm width) showed $\sim97.5\%$ yield across $2000$ structures. CPW resonators exhibited median $Q_i^{\mathrm{LP}} \approx 4.3 \times 10^5$ with loss per grounding airbridge $\sim 2.3 \times 10^{-8}$ (two orders of magnitude below intrinsic loss). Transmons showed median $T_1 \sim 100$ µs across chips, with peak values $\sim 290$ µs, comparable to state-of-the-art all-Al devices.
